title: the clearance proof builds its trace path through trace_path, not by hand
intention: test_clearance.py names the clearance queue file through learning_block.trace_path, so it reads the file the writer actually wrote on every box.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: lines 379 and 394 of test_clearance.py read f"{QUEUE_BLOCK}.jsonl"; the proof fails on akiendell, baseline included
traces_to: Law 3 and Law 8: a proof that is red on one box for a naming reason, not a behaviour reason, is not measuring the component; CP4 resolves the chafe.
how: Replace the two f-string paths at lines 379 and 394 with trace_path(QUEUE_BLOCK, root=...) and re-run the proof on akiendell.

clauses.claim: test_clearance.py contains no hand-built trace file name for QUEUE_BLOCK (git grep finds none)
test_clearance.py runs green on a Windows box

decisions.text: D2: one proof, one tooth per clause; red first.

measured.saw: lines 379 and 394 of test_clearance.py read f"{QUEUE_BLOCK}.jsonl"; the proof fails on akiendell, baseline included
measured.how: git grep -n QUEUE_BLOCK over the proof file; a plain python run
